state.purpose: Attack the commoditization weakness of cloud-cost-savings-refresh by changing value capture, not by adding product scope. Optimize for highest realized owner hourly earnings reached quickly.

marketEvidence: ProsperOps publicly prices Autonomous Discount Management as a small percentage of realized cloud savings rather than cloud spend.
nOps describes commitment optimization as a share-of-savings business model and offers a free savings analysis.
ProsperOps+ publicly extends outcome-based pricing across a broader FinOps suite, arguing that pricing tied to optimization outcomes makes ROI clear.
AWS reports that visibility alone is insufficient for many organizations because teams struggle to turn identified savings into action.
caveats: Outcome-based pricing is validated in the category, but established competitors often execute or automate the optimization itself.
This proposed service does not execute customer infrastructure changes, so attribution of realized savings may be weaker.
Public vendor claims do not prove this entrant can win customers.

candidates.name: fixed-audit-annual-refresh
candidates.claim: Keep X3 unchanged commercially: one prepaid bounded cloud-cost savings audit, then optional prepaid annual plan with up to four refreshes. Customer executes all actions. Price is fixed and unrelated to realized savings.

candidates.name: pure-savings-share
candidates.claim: Run the bounded cloud-cost audit with no upfront fee. Customer pays an agreed share only on independently verifiable first-year savings from customer-executed actions that originated in the audit. Reruns are included only while the savings-share agreement is active.

candidates.name: paid-audit-plus-savings-share
candidates.claim: Charge a fixed prepaid fee for the bounded audit to cover analysis and establish first cash. If the customer implements an identified action, charge an additional agreed share of independently verifiable first-year savings. If the customer converts to the prepaid annual refresh plan, the initial audit schema and savings receipt remain unchanged. Customer executes all effects.

candidates.name: paid-audit-credit-to-outcome-contract
candidates.claim: Charge a fixed prepaid audit fee. After the audit, the customer may convert to an outcome contract where the audit fee is credited against future savings-share charges. The service refreshes the same analysis up to four times per year; the customer executes all actions and reports verifiable realized savings.

candidates.name: fixed-fee-with-verified-savings-tier
candidates.claim: Charge a fixed prepaid audit fee with no percentage share. The next annual-refresh price tier is determined by verified savings found in the previous period: higher verified value supports a higher fixed renewal price. Customer executes all actions; no contingent fee collection is required.

constraints: Do not add execution authority, infrastructure changes, or new product modules.
First paid work must remain a bounded file/export-based audit.
Savings attribution must be based on observable customer billing/readback, not self-reported vague value.
No full SaaS platform before repeated paid demand.
